advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen or narrow `test_real_review_run_evidence_is_committed` so it asserts a real contract (e.g. a canonical run-invocation token a parser would key on) rather than existence plus free-prose substrings, or downgrade it to a pure existence check acknowledged as such.
evidence: assert CRITERION_ID in body and "review-plan" in body, ("the evidence file must show a real review-plan run naming the criterion")
The grepped doc is human prose (docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md), not an artifact read by a parser/validator/registry — an LLM/human reader is not a non-human consumer.
Refactoring-violation criterion: rewording the doc (e.g. hyphen -> space in 'review-plan') breaks the test with no observable-behavior change.
advisory.finding: `test_real_review_run_evidence_is_committed` asserts only that a human-readable docs file exists and contains the substrings `CRITERION_ID` and `"review-plan"`. No non-human consumer parses `docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md`, so this is an existence + prose-substring change-detector: it would break on a behavior-neutral rewording (e.g. `review-plan` -> `review plan`) and verifies no code behavior. It cannot detect a regression in the criterion/move wiring the diff introduces.
scenarios: A future edit rephrases the sample doc heading/prose, breaking CI though nothing about the criterion or move behavior changed.
Conversely, the criterion/move wiring could regress while the doc still contains the two substrings, and this test would stay green — regression blindness.
